paragraflar: Merkezi ve Yayincilik Hizmetleri 1 Did you know that animals are also each other? Bees communicate by dancing. Whales talk to each other by singing. And some apes talk to humans by using American Sign 2 Meet Koko: a female gorilla born at the San Francisco Zoo on July 4th, 1971. Koko learned sign language from, Dr. Penny Patterson. Patterson began teaching sign language to Koko in 1972, when Koko was one year old. Koko was a good student for sure, so she moved onto the Stanford University campus with Dr. Patterson. Koko continued to learn on the campus until 1976. That's when full-time with Patterson's group, the Gorilla Foundation. The relationship between Patterson and Koko has blossomed ever since. 3 Dr. Patterson says that Koko has mastered sign language. She says that Koko knows over 1,000 words, and that Koko makes up new words. For example, Koko didn't know the sign for ring, so she signed the words finger and bracelet. Dr. Patterson thinks that this shows meaningful and constructive use of language. 4 Not everyone agrees with. Patterson. Some argue that apes like Koko do not understand the meaning of what they are doing. Skeptics say that these apes are just performing complex tricks. For example, if an apple and signs red or apple, Dr. Patterson will give her an apple. They argue that Koko does not really know what means. She only knows that if she makes the right motion, then apple. The debate is unsolved, but for certain: Koko is an extraordinary ape. drainer Adtesadi?
